header:
Draws a solid line from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2), the four words the caller pushed (x1 pushed last), by filling the op-00 record buffer at 0x06CA and calling SeGfx_StaticOp00_FromBuf; preserves every register, caller pops the 8 bytes.
Basis: callers + body -- the graph drawers (SeMenu_DrawKeyScaleGraph, SeMenu_DrawFilterGraph, SeMenu_DrawBandPassCurve) push four coordinates and call it for axes and curve segments.
evidence: audio/semenu_routines.s:4713 `pushw 97` / 4714 `pushw 254` / 4715 `pushw 97` / 4716 `pushw 48` / 4717 `call SeMenu_ApplyPartEdit_AltStore_Helper` -- SeMenu_DrawKeyScaleGraph: x1=48,y1=97,x2=254,y2=97, a horizontal axis
audio/semenu_routines.s:5392 `pushm (xsp+12)` .. 5396 `call SeMenu_ApplyPartEdit_AltStore_Helper` / 5397 `inc 8, xsp` -- SeMenu_DrawBandPassCurve pushes 4 words and pops them itself

audio/sound_editor_ui.s:8020 `ld wa, (xiz+8)` / 8021 `ld (1740:16), wa` .. 8026 `ld wa, (xiz+14)` / 8027 `ld (1746:16), wa` -- the 4 stacked words go to record fields 0x6CC..0x6D2 (+2..+8 of the record at 0x6CA)
audio/sound_editor_ui.s:8029 `call SeGfx_StaticOp00_FromBuf` -- 7783 `ld xwa, 0x000006ca` / 7784 `call SeGfx_StaticOp00_Line`
display/graphics_text_vga.s:685 `ld bc, (xde+2)` .. 692 `ld de, (xde+8)` / 695 `calr DrawLineWithMode` -- op 00 draws a line between (+2,+4) and (+6,+8)
note: SeMenu_ApplyPartEdit_AltStore_Helper2 (audio/sound_editor_ui.s:8038) is the same wrapper for op 15 (SeGfx_StaticOp15_DottedLine)

header:
Steps the bit field of edit record XWA (+0 old byte, +6 mask, +7 shift, +8 max, +9 min, +10 signed step) by the step, clamped to [min,max], and writes the merged byte to +3; L = 1 if the field changed, 0 if not or if the record is unusable (mask 0, shift > 7, step 0). min < 0 takes the signed-compare copy.
Basis: callers + body -- the OnColumn handlers fill +6..+10 (SeMenu_SwitchToValueStep writes +10) and test L; SeMenu_StepParamFieldAndSend wraps it and sends the byte at +3.
evidence: audio/semenu_routines.s:6655 `ld (xbc+6), 31` .. 6658 `ld (xbc+9), 0` / 6662 `call SeMenu_SwitchToValueStep` / 6664 `call SeMenu_TransferPartValues_EndData_Helper` / 6665 `cp l, 1:i3` -- SePitPit1_OnColumn6 builds the record and tests L
audio/semenu_routines.s:1702-1705 header of SeMenu_StepParamFieldAndSend (+0 value, +6 mask, +7 shift, +8 max, +9 min, +10 step) / 1714 `calr SeMenu_TransferPartValues_EndData_Helper`
audio/semenu_routines.s:1733 `lda xde, (xiz+3)` / 1745 `ld c, (xiz+3)` -- the caller reads the new byte from +3
audio/semenu_routines.s:1216 `cp (xwa+6), 0` / 1218 `cp (xwa+7), 7` / 1220 `cp (xwa+10), 0` / 1223 `ld l, 0:opc` -- unusable record -> L = 0
audio/semenu_routines.s:1226 `cp (xwa+9), 0` / 1228 `calr SeMenu_TransferPartValues_EndData_Helper_Helper` / 1231 `calr SeMenu_TransferPartValues_EndData_Helper_Helper2` -- min >= 0 vs signed path
audio/semenu_routines.s:1238 `lda xbc, (xwa+3)` / 1290 `ld (xwa), l` / 1292 `or (xwa), c` / 1293 `ld hl, 1:i3` -- (value & mask) << shift merged with the other bits into +3, returns 1

header:
Reads fields 12, 13 and 14 of the active MIDI message as three 7-bit bytes (MSB first), forms the 21-bit length N, and sets both transfer descriptors at 0xBCDC and 0xBCEC to {+4 = base(+0) + N, +8 = N}.
Basis: callers + body -- MidiPkt_ArpExtHandler_G/J/M_Data first point the 0xBCEC descriptor at a fixed buffer (base, base+size, size), then call it so the expected byte count comes from the message.
evidence: midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:11582 `ld xwa, 0xbcec` / 11583 `call MidiPkt_ArpPopReturn_Helper7` / 11584 `call MidiPkt_ArpExtHandler_G_Helper` -- MidiPkt_ArpExtHandler_G (field 3 = 9); _J (11628-11630) and _M_Data (11673-11675) do the same
midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:10183 `lda xwa, (0x95bc0:24)` / 10185 `add xwa, 0x15440` / 10186 `ld (xiz+4), xwa` / 10188 `ld (xiz+8), xwa` -- the descriptor layout {base, base+size, size}
midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:10017 `ldw bc, 12` / 10021 `sll xiz, 14` / 10023 `ldw bc, 13` / 10027 `sll xhl, 7` / 10030 `ldw bc, 14` / 10034 `or xiz, xhl` -- N = f12<<14 | f13<<7 | f14
midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:10035 `lda xwa, (0xbcdc:16)` / 10037 `add xbc, xiz` / 10038 `ld (xwa+4), xbc` / 10039 `ld (xwa+8), xiz` -- same for 0xBCEC at 10040-10044

midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:9963 `lda xiy, (0xbcec:16)` / 9967 `inc 8, xiy` / 9986 `ld (xiz), c` / 9992 `ld (xiy), xbc` -- SeqVoice_DispatchProcess_Data writes decoded bytes through 0xBCEC+0 and counts +8 down (also 0xBCDC+8 at 9965/9989)

header:
Queues a part volume: for target BC with part C <= 31 it stores E | 0x80 in the pending-volume byte 0x94B2[C]; target BC = 0x00B0 instead marks 0x90F8, stores E in MIDI_CC_EXPRESSION_PENDING and calls Audio_WriteBankSelectParams at once.
Basis: callers + body -- MidiCC_RxCC7_Volume passes its CC7 target (function 3, the part) and PerfMode_Evt04_VolumeHandler passes C = PART_SELECT, B = 3; the scanners send each flagged byte as function 3.
evidence: midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:554 `ld xix, MidiCC_PartTargets_CC7_Volume` / 555 `ld bc, (xix+hl)` / 560 `ld e, (38454:16)` / 565 `call PerfMode_Evt04_VolumeHandler_Helper2` -- CC7 handler
midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:2289 `.byte 0x00, 0x03, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x03, 0x7f, 0x02, 0x03, 0x7f, 0x03, 0x03, 0x7f` -- CC7 targets are {C = part, B = 3, mask 0x7F}
display/scoop_display.s:1792 `ld c, e` / 1793 `ld b, 3:opc` / 1794 `ld e, (3831:16)` / 1796 `call PerfMode_Evt04_VolumeHandler_Helper2` -- PerfMode volume event, C = PART_SELECT
audio/audio_control_engine.s:10995 `cp c, 31` / 10997 `set 7, e` / 10998 `ld xix, 0x94b2` / 10999 `ld (xix+c), e` -- pending flag + value per part
audio/audio_control_engine.s:10993 `cp bc, 176` / 11003 `ld (MIDI_CC_EXPRESSION_PENDING:16), e` / 11004 `call Audio_WriteBankSelectParams` -- the 0x00B0 target

header:
Locates the current rhythm's header in the Rhythm Data ROM (RhythmROM_BankProgramLocators[bank 0xFC5B & 0x7F][program 0xFC5A], 0x400000 + (hi & 0xFF) << 16 + lo) and copies its byte +976 (0x3D0), the time-signature index into TimeSig_DisplayStrings, to RAM 0x34F0.
Basis: callers + body + ROM data -- every rhythm-selection path (DrumVoice_Handler6/7, RhythmVariation_Select_Entry_Data, AccPatch_CallParamLookup_Helper) calls it after the selection.
evidence: sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25494 `calr DrumVoice_Handler6_Helper` / 25495 `calr DrumKit_PostMidiEvents` / 25496 `calr RhythmVariation_Select_Helper` -- DrumVoice_Handler6 (Handler7 25508-25510 the same)
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25226 `calr RhythmVariation_Select_Helper` -- RhythmVariation_Select_Entry_Data, after storing the new program/bank
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25840 `ld l, (0xfc5a:16)` / 25842 `ld h, (0xfc5b:16)` / 25846 `ld xiy, RhythmROM_BankProgramLocators` / 25854 `ld xix, 0x400000` -- header address
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25859 `ld a, (xix+976)` / 25860 `ld (0x34f0:16), a`

probe ~/compartilhado/tmp/kn5000-naming/agent_d/rhythm_probe.py on kn5000_rhythm_data_rom.ic14: of 201 non-zero locators, +976 = 7 (186x), 6 (13x), 9 (1x), 11 (1x); the 6s are waltz/mazurka headers (wzs87e1n, wzv32n1n, jwf56k1n, mzr27d1n ...), the 11 is '8beats1n'
sequencer/accompaniment_engine.s:25956 TimeSig_DisplayStrings, 10-byte records: index 6 = "(3/4)+0", 7 = "(4/4)+0", 9 = "(6/4)+0", 11 = "(8/4)+0"

caveat: the only reader of 0x34F0 (DrumVoice_Handler7_Helper_Helper, 25902 `ld l, (0x34f0:16)`) indexes TimeSig_DisplayStrings+7 with stride 8, which does not fit the 10-byte records (already flagged at 25964-25968)

header:
Writes up to count bytes from buffer to file handle (stack args handle, buffer, count, line_mode) at its position (+22) through the sector buffer, marking the handle dirty (+3 bit 7) and the entry's archive bit (+64 bit 5); text mode (+3 bit 2) expands LF to CR LF, line_mode stops after the terminator byte (+2); extends the size (+71). Returns HL = bytes written.
Basis: callers + body -- it is the body of drive A's file-op slots 3 and 4 (SeqChan_ProcessEventArg0/1, line_mode 0/1) in FileIO_DriveAFileOps.
evidence: v10/maincpu/ui_widgets/naka_sequencer_channels.c:2821 `NAKA_ADDR(SeqByteBlock_ChannelContainer), NAKA_ADDR(SeqChan_SetupAndCallHelper), NAKA_ADDR(SeqChan_InitChannelState), NAKA_ADDR(SeqChan_ProcessEventArg0),` -- FileIO_DriveAFileOps (ui_widgets/sequencer_channel_containers.s:81-84: the drive-A file-op table)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7491 `SeqChan_ProcessEventArg0:` / 7492 `pushw 0` / 7498 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper10`; 7502 `pushw 1` / 7508 in SeqChan_ProcessEventArg1
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7253 `setm 7, (xwa+3)` / 7255 `setm 5, (xwa+64)` -- dirty + archive attribute
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7348 `call Mem_Copy` (buffer -> sector buffer +26) / 7358 `add (xwa+22), xbc` -- advances the position
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7422 `cp (xwa), 10` / 7424 `ld (xde+), 13` / 7412 `ld (xde+), 10` -- text mode LF -> CR LF
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7446 `ld a, (xwa+2)` / 7447 `cp a, (xde+)` -- line_mode stops at the terminator
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7463 `cp xbc, (xwa+71)` / 7468 `ld (xbc+71), xwa` -- size grows to the position

header:
Frees the cluster chain of the file handle on the stack: from its first cluster (+69) it reads each next link (Fat_ReadEntry) and writes 0 into the FAT entry, until a link is 0 or above (volume +36) - 8; unless handle +3 bit 5 is set it then zeroes +69, +42 and the file size +71.
Basis: callers + body -- the file-op slot 9 handler (SeqChan_WriteExtendedPatch) calls it for request 21 before writing 0xE5 (deleted) into the entry; the open path calls it when the truncate flag (+3 bit 4) is set.
evidence: sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7768 `SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Skip32:` / 7770 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper5` / 7772 `ld (xiz+52), 229` -- delete: free clusters, mark the entry 0xE5

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6592 `bitm 4, (xwa+3)` / 6596 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper5` -- SeqByteBlock_ChannelContainer (open): truncate flag; 6584-6589 bit 3 sets position = size (+71)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6030 `ld iz, (xwa+69)` / 6039 `calr Fat_ReadEntry` / 6045 `calr SeqStep_FileSectorPopReturn` (pushw 0, pushw iz) -- next link, then FAT[cluster] = 0
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:4833-4858 SeqStep_FileSectorPopReturn: FAT12/16 entry offset n*3/2 or 2n in the FAT sector (the write side of Fat_ReadEntry, header 4707-4714)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6053 `ld wa, (xwa+36)` / 6054 `dec 8, wa` / 6055 `cp iz, wa` / 6056 `jr ule, SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Loop10` -- stop at end/bad marks
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6059 `bitm 5, (xwa+3)` / 6062 `ldw (xwa+69), 0` / 6065 `ld (xwa+42), bc` / 6068 `ld (xwa+71), xbc`

header:
Reads up to count bytes from file handle into buffer (stack args handle, buffer, count, line_mode) from its position (+22), clamped to the size (+71); at end of file sets the EOF flag (+6 |= 0x8000) and returns 0; text mode (+3 bit 2) drops CRs, line_mode stops after the terminator byte (+2). Returns HL = bytes read.
